name: Nullweave Tier-4 Chrome-Display Office Suit
description: For the augmented professional who has stopped hiding their chrome and started wearing it as a credential. The Nullweave Tier-4 Chrome-Display Office Suit is cut from a deep navy stretch-woven fabric with a matte finish that reads as formal from across a meeting room but moves like a second skin. The jacket is structured at the shoulder but open-seamed along the left sleeve from mid-bicep to wrist — a deliberate aug-display cut that lets chrome forearm and wrist installations be seen without removing the jacket. The open seam is finished with a brushed gunmetal trim that echoes the chrome it frames, creating the impression that the suit was designed around the augmentation rather than adapted for it. It was. The right sleeve is fully closed, traditional, creating an asymmetry that reads as intentional style rather than accommodation. Underneath, a fitted Nullweave mock-neck base shirt in slate-grey with a rear neural port channel — a clean slot at the base of the collar that sits open, allowing BCI port access without disturbing the shirt's line. Trousers are slim-tapered in matching navy stretch-woven, with a hidden inner-thigh seam channel for lower-limb chrome routing, sealed with a micro-zip along the inner leg. Footwear is a pair of matte-black side-zip ankle boots with a reinforced toe cap — practical, grounded, and just formatted enough to pass a Tier 4 dress code audit. The aug-display cut telegraphs a specific message in corporate culture: this person's chrome is not a disability accommodation, it is a qualification.
functionality: Aug-display open seam on left sleeve with gunmetal trim framing, rear neural port channel in mock-neck collar, inner-thigh chrome routing channel with micro-zip, stretch fabric for full range of motion with prosthetic limbs, BCI-transparent fabric (does not interfere with active implant signals)
what_it_says: The wearer has augmentation worth showing. In Tier 4 corporate culture, visible chrome signals that you are a specialist — the kind of person whose modifications were expensive and purposeful, not cosmetic. The asymmetric sleeve cut says this person is aware of fashion and has made a deliberate choice, which signals taste on top of capability. They are not ashamed of what they've had installed, and they want you to wonder what it does.
worn_by: augmented analysts at corponations with visible-aug cultures
story_hooks: The aug-display cut was designed to show a standard forearm installation, but the wearer has something unusual in that sleeve — a non-registered modification that a sharp-eyed Tier 5 executive clocks halfway through a presentation, and doesn't mention until the meeting is over.

A Tier 3 worker saves up for six months to buy this suit secondhand, hoping the aug-display cut will help them pass as Tier 4 in a job interview — the chrome they're displaying is a basic port, not the specialist rig the suit implies, and the interviewer knows the difference.

The BCI-transparent fabric is exactly why this suit was chosen for a covert operation — the wearer needs their active implants to transmit without the building's signal-suppression field detecting a breach, and the Nullweave passes through cleanly.
